original_poem:
ஆசையின் கோவில்,  
உன் உள்ளத்தில் எழுந்தது,  
என் இதயத்தின் தேவதை,  
காதலின் கடலில் அலைகிறது!
translated_poem:
Temple of desire,  
Emerged in your heart,  
The angel of my soul,  
Waves in the sea of love!

stanzas.loss_note: தேவதை (tevatai) in Tamil carries the specific weight of a tutelary deity or divine feminine presence, not merely 'angel'; the translation loses the devotional-sacred register and flattens it into a generic English spiritual term.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the beloved's heart as a consecrated space for desire
the soul-deity adrift and unmoored in the vastness of love

cultural_entities.translation_note: Rendered as 'temple' which is accurate lexically, but the kovil in Tamil devotional imagination is not merely a building — it is the dwelling-place of the divine, making the metaphor of the beloved's heart as kovil a theologically charged image that 'temple' only partially conveys.
Rendered as 'angel', losing the Tamil devotional specificity of tevatai as a divine feminine tutelary presence distinct from the Abrahamic angel concept.
